'''Faster Boot Sequence''' is an [[Engineering Blueprints|Engineering Blueprint]] for [[Frame Shift Drive|Frame Shift Drives]]. It shortens the time an FSD takes to become operational after the module is powered on or restored from a disabled state. It also increases optimized mass, but by less than the [[Increased Range]] Blueprint.<ref name="inara">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/1/ Frame Shift Drive – Faster boot sequence], INARA.</ref>

{{#invoke:EngineeringBlueprints|infobox|fsd_faster_boot_sequence}}

== Effects and trade-offs ==

The Blueprint scales through Grades 1–5. Higher grades progressively:

* reduce boot time;
* increase optimized mass, providing a modest jump-range benefit;
* increase thermal load; and
* reduce module integrity.

The boot-time modifier applies to the module's startup sequence. It does not shorten the normal FSD charging countdown for supercruise or hyperspace jumps.

{{#invoke:EngineeringBlueprints|gradeTable|fsd_faster_boot_sequence}}

== Selection considerations ==

Faster Boot Sequence is most relevant when an FSD is deliberately disabled by power priorities or must recover quickly after being shut down. Power-managed combat and utility builds can use the shorter startup delay to bring the drive back online sooner when it is needed.

For ships whose priority is maximum jump range, [[Increased Range]] provides a substantially larger optimized-mass bonus. Faster Boot Sequence is the narrower choice when startup delay matters and a smaller secondary range increase is still useful.

The integrity and thermal penalties make it less attractive when module durability or heat management is already constrained. A compatible [[Experimental Effects|Experimental Effect]] can adjust some of those priorities, but only one Experimental Effect may be installed on the drive.

== Availability ==

{{#invoke:EngineeringBlueprints|engineers|fsd_faster_boot_sequence}}

Blueprint grades can be applied through [[Remote Engineering]] after the Blueprint is pinned and the required Engineer access has been earned. Experimental Effects still require a visit to an Engineer workshop.
